summary: Neo Delay in Stereo mode with its filters open: the first track's Length (in its unit) becomes Sync and Feel, or a free Time; Feedback carries over to ±99 %; Dry thru and Wet out become a crossfade and an output gain.

rules.why: Lengths count in Length unit: ticks (the default) are Buzz's whole samples per tick, so the echo follows the tempo; a length in ticks that is a note value (1 tick = 1/16 at 4 ticks a beat, 3 ticks = 1/8 dotted, 6 = 1/4 dotted …) becomes Neo Delay's Sync and Feel, which follow the tempo too; any other length, and lengths in ms or samples, a free Time at the song's tempo and rate.
Both in % of each echo fed back (Jeskola Delay's source: buf = in + fb · buf, (raw − 64)/64); Neo Delay's stops at ±99 %, where Jeskola's ±100 % never decays.
Jeskola Delay adds the dry signal (on or off) and its echoes at Wet out (raw/128); Neo Delay crossfades them and sets the output's level: mix = wet ÷ (dry + wet), output = dry + wet.

remarks: Jeskola Delay is mono: ReBuzz gives it left + right summed (+6 dB for a centred sound) and it plays the same on both sides; Neo Delay in Stereo mode keeps the input's image, so a centred sound is the same and a panned one stays where it is. The +6 dB goes on the output connections, not the inputs: the line keeps the input's own level, under its saturator's knee (0 dBFS at Drive 0 dB), as Jeskola Delay's float line never saturates.

Each of Jeskola Delay's tracks is a tap of its own (up to 8); Neo Delay has one line a side: the first track's settings move, the others' are left out (their pattern columns write the same parameters, with a note).
Jeskola Delay's Max Delay attribute (1 s by default) caps its lengths; the mapping doesn't read attributes, so a longer length plays longer on Neo Delay (up to 5 s free, 10 s synced).
